section_summary: This section details the custody, liquidation, and investigation of Japanese diplomatic property and public archives across various countries following the Second World War, including Italy, Chile, Peru, Canada, and South Africa. A substantial portion consists of an Italian auction catalogue liquidating furniture, artwork, office supplies, and fine wines from the former Japanese Embassy in Rome under the supervision of Allied authorities. The records also document Allied diplomatic coordination regarding powers of attorney granted to Vatican attorney Giulio Dante, proposals for Four-Power policy on consular archives, and Counter Intelligence Corps findings that the Japanese Foreign Office deciphered 1941 State Department telegrams using a cipher key stolen from the American Consulate in Taihoku.

subfiles.about: Auction catalogue listing furnishings, art objects, office equipment, and personal effects from the former Japanese Embassy in Rome for public sale.
subfiles.summary: Italian auction catalogue detailing lots 151 through 763 sold across the third through ninth days of public sale from September 25 to October 2, 1946, in Rome. The catalogued property from the former Japanese Embassy includes office furniture, carpets, Japanese and Chinese artwork, European paintings, fine wines, and kitchenware. Printed by Arti Grafiche Mariti & Majone in Rome.
subfiles.title: Italian Auction Catalogue for Sale of Japanese Embassy Furnishings and Effects in Rome (Days 3 to 9)

subfiles.about: Reports the departure of the Nisei microfilming team from Rome and requests that any further microfilming requests be submitted by August 20.
subfiles.summary: EmbOff Key reports all but one Nisei microfilmer have returned to the U.S., with the last leaving around August 20.
subfiles.title: Incoming Telegram No. 3342 from Rome regarding Return of Nisei Microfilm Team

subfiles.about: Reports on the legal authorization of Vatican attorney Giulio Dante to take custody of Japanese embassy and civilian effects in Rome.
subfiles.summary: Key reports Allied embassies confirmed attorney Giulio Dante's power of attorney, allowing removal of Japanese effects to restore the villa to owners.
subfiles.title: Incoming Airgram A-799 from Rome regarding Legal Authority of Giulio Dante over Japanese Property

subfiles.about: Authorizes dropping Point 6 from previous instructions and requests a copy of the shipment manifest for Japanese property.
subfiles.summary: Acheson instructs Embassy Rome to drop Point 6 and forward a manifest of the Japanese property shipment.
subfiles.title: Outgoing Telegram No. 1589 to Rome regarding Japanese Property Manifest

subfiles.about: Duplicate record copy of Airgram A-799 reporting on Giulio Dante's authority to assume custody of Japanese effects in Rome.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate copy of Rome Airgram A-799 confirming attorney Giulio Dante's authority to assume custody of Japanese embassy and civilian property.
subfiles.title: Incoming Airgram A-799 from Rome regarding Custody of Japanese Property (Duplicate Copy)

subfiles.about: Reports that the Japanese Foreign Office confirmed Kiuchi's power of attorney to Dante and is ready to confirm Kanayama's.
subfiles.summary: Atcheson reports the Japanese Foreign Office confirms Yoshitane Kiuchi's power of attorney to Giulio Dante as authentic and binding.
subfiles.title: Incoming Telegram No. 359 from Tokyo regarding Powers of Attorney for Giulio Dante (Action Copy)

subfiles.about: Information copy of telegram reporting Japanese Foreign Office confirmation of powers of attorney issued to Giulio Dante.
subfiles.summary: Information copy of Tokyo Telegram 359 confirming the validity of Kiuchi's power of attorney granted to Giulio Dante.
subfiles.title: Incoming Telegram No. 359 from Tokyo regarding Powers of Attorney for Giulio Dante (Information Copy)

subfiles.about: Advises against shipping German and Japanese archives to Berlin or Tokyo and instructs that they be kept intact in Tehran.
subfiles.summary: Acheson advises that shipping archives is impractical and instructs Tehran to keep German and Japanese archives intact locally.
subfiles.title: Outgoing Airgram A-122 to Tehran regarding Disposition and Exploitation of German and Japanese Archives

subfiles.about: Department routing slip directing Santiago Despatch No. 14,304 to ARA and other divisions.
subfiles.summary: Department routing slip directing Santiago Despatch 14,304 regarding Japanese archives and property to ARA, JA, OCD, and SPD.
subfiles.title: DC/R Routing Slip for Despatch No. 14,304 from Santiago

subfiles.about: Reports on Soviet inquiries regarding Japanese archives and property in Chile, enclosing a memorandum of conversation with Soviet First Secretary Mukhin.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Bowers forwards a memorandum detailing discussions with Soviet First Secretary Mukhin regarding Japanese legation premises, archives, and bank accounts in Chile. Reed clarified that former Japanese quarters were leased and sold to China, and Minister Yamagata's diary was available for perusal.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 14,304 from Santiago enclosing Memorandum of Conversation regarding Japanese Archives and Property in Chile

subfiles.about: Transmits commercial documents and papers obtained from the former Japanese Legation files in Lima.
subfiles.summary: Cover despatch from Lima submitting commercial transaction files obtained from the former Japanese Legation in Peru.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 235 from Lima transmitting Commercial Documents from Japanese Legation Files

subfiles.about: Proposes coordinated Four-Power principles for managing and disposing of Japanese consular archives, official property, and personal effects abroad.
subfiles.summary: Acheson proposes Four-Power principles for administering Japanese diplomatic and consular property and archives abroad to minimize administrative burdens.
subfiles.title: Outgoing Telegram No. 6148 to London regarding Four-Power Policy for Japanese Archives and Property

subfiles.about: Sets forth the specific draft text to be presented to the Japanese Government regarding the administration and preservation of consular archives.
subfiles.summary: Outgoing telegram containing proposed text informing Japan of Four-Power terms governing the preservation and storage costs of consular archives.
subfiles.title: Outgoing Telegram No. 6149 to London containing Proposed Text for Presentation to Japanese Government

subfiles.about: Department routing slip directing Mexico Despatch No. 786 to FC and other offices.
subfiles.summary: Department routing slip routing Mexico Despatch 786 to FC, ARA, JA, OCD, CIG, War, and Navy.
subfiles.title: DC/R Routing Slip for Despatch No. 786 from Mexico

subfiles.about: Department routing slip routing Tokyo Despatch No. 581 to FC and intelligence agencies.
subfiles.summary: Department routing slip routing Tokyo Despatch 581 regarding Japanese possession of State Department documents to FC and military intelligence.
subfiles.title: DC/R Routing Slip for Despatch No. 581 from Tokyo

subfiles.about: Transmits Counter Intelligence Corps investigations and decoded Moscow telegrams revealing that the Japanese Foreign Office obtained State Department telegrams using a cipher key stolen from the Taihoku Consulate.
subfiles.summary: Political Adviser George Atcheson, Jr. forwards Counter Intelligence Corps reports and SCAP International Prosecution Section evidentiary documents concerning State Department telegrams recovered from Japanese Foreign Office files. Investigations revealed that Japanese Military Police stole a cipher key from the American Consulate in Taihoku, Formosa, enabling the Japanese "Black Chamber" to decode low-classification communications. Attached are decoded copies of Ambassador Steinhardt's April 1941 Moscow telegrams reporting on Foreign Minister Matsuoka's conferences with Hitler, Ribbentrop, and Molotov, and the conclusion of the Soviet-Japanese Neutrality Pact.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 581 from Tokyo enclosing Reports and Decoded Telegrams regarding Compromised Cipher Key and State Department Documents

subfiles.about: Conveys the British Foreign Office's views and concurrence on the proposed Four-Power text and policy for Japanese archives and property.
subfiles.summary: Gallman reports the British Foreign Office agrees to preserve archives intact, accepts selling official property to preserve value, and concurs with proposed terms.
subfiles.title: Incoming Telegram No. 7894 from London regarding British Views on Japanese Archives and Property

subfiles.about: Explains efforts to harmonize British and U.S. views with China and the USSR and confirms property may be sold to preserve value.
subfiles.summary: Acheson explains the proposed policy harmonizes British and U.S. views to prevent friction and confirms property may be sold to preserve value.
subfiles.title: Outgoing Airgram A-2403 to London regarding Coordination of Policy on Japanese Archives and Property

subfiles.about: Requests clarification whether the British concur with all points under paragraph A of the proposed text on archives.
subfiles.summary: Acheson asks Embassy London to clarify whether the British Foreign Office concurs with all four points on archives or only point three.
subfiles.title: Outgoing Airgram to London requesting Clarification of British Concurrence on Archives

subfiles.about: Transmits Ottawa Despatch No. 4314 reporting on the joint U.S.-Canadian examination of Japanese consular archives from Vancouver.
subfiles.summary: Bradford transmits an Ottawa Embassy report on the joint U.S.-Canadian examination of archives recovered from the Japanese Consulate in Vancouver.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from FC to G-2 transmitting Report on Japanese Consular Archives in Canada

subfiles.about: Transmits Ottawa Despatch No. 4314 concerning the examination of Japanese consular archives from Vancouver.
subfiles.summary: Cummings transmits a copy of Ottawa Despatch 4314 regarding the examination of Vancouver Japanese consular archives to the Captured Documents Center.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from FC to Captured Documents Center transmitting Report on Japanese Archives in Canada

subfiles.about: Contains diplomatic notes between the American Legation and South African authorities regarding the inspection and contents of Japanese archives in South Africa.
subfiles.summary: Enclosed diplomatic notes from Pretoria: the U.S. Legation requested access to inspect Japanese archives, and South African authorities replied that examining former Japanese legation and consular archives in Pretoria and Cape Town disclosed only routine commercial correspondence, reference books, travel films, and stationery.
subfiles.title: Enclosures to Despatch No. 1063 from Pretoria regarding Japanese Archives in the Union of South Africa

subfiles.about: Department routing slip routing Pretoria Despatch No. 1063 to FC, FE, and intelligence agencies.
subfiles.summary: Department routing slip routing Pretoria Despatch 1063 regarding Japanese archives in South Africa to FC, JA, OCD, and military agencies.
subfiles.title: DC/R Routing Slip for Despatch No. 1063 from Pretoria
